# Results — Study 383 (SOFR-Repo-Stress)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore — **a spike in
overnight repo / SOFR is a forward warning for risk assets** — tested against a
**hardcoded, sourced table of named repo-stress episodes**. There is no free, clean daily
SOFR / repo-spread tape on yfinance, so the *signal* is the curated list of well-documented
funding-stress dates (Sept 2019, the quarter/year-end turns, March 2020, SVB 2023, …) and
we measure the forward reaction of **SPY** (equities) and **HYG / LQD** (credit) around
each, vs the unconditional base rate. 1-day entry lag, Welch t, placebo null. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — SPY, HYG, LQD (public, no key) |
| Window | 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-18 (**4,140** trading days; **16.5** years) |
| Signal | **13** hardcoded, sourced repo/funding-stress episode dates (see `data.REPO_EPISODES`) |
| Event rule | enter the risk asset **1 trading day after** the stress date; hold 5 / 20 / 60 days |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag; one round-trip cost of 5 bps on the de-risking trade |

> **Signal caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The repo-stress dates are a **curated,
> hardcoded list**, not a mechanical threshold on a live SOFR feed (which isn't free on
> yfinance). The list is deliberately *generous* — it folds in the routine quarter- and
> year-end funding turns alongside the famous systemic events — to make the event count
> (and therefore the test) as large as honesty allows. Even so it is **13 episodes in 16.5
> years**, and the verdict does not hinge on the exact list: any ~once-a-year-or-rarer
> named-event signal is statistically underpowered, which holds *a fortiori* for the
> handful of truly systemic repo crises.

## The signal — forward returns after a repo spike vs the base rate

1-day entry lag; the unconditional column is *all* overlapping forward windows over the
same tape (the honest base rate). A **negative** Welch *t* is the believer's wanted sign
(risk assets do *worse* after a spike); the placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 random
same-size date draws that are at least as **bearish** as the episode set (left tail).

**SPY (equities)**

| horizon | n | cond. mean | cond. P[down] | base mean | base P[down] | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 13 | **−0.71%** | 46% | +0.29% | 39% | **−0.96** | 0.059 |
| 20-day | 13 | **+1.95%** | 46% | +1.16% | 31% | **+0.62** | 0.755 |
| 60-day | 13 | **+5.21%** | 23% | +3.41% | 23% | **+0.66** | 0.849 |

**HYG (high-yield credit)**

| horizon | n | cond. mean | cond. P[down] | base mean | base P[down] | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 13 | **−0.61%** | 54% | +0.11% | 40% | **−1.09** | 0.024 |
| 20-day | 13 | **+1.06%** | 54% | +0.43% | 34% | **+0.91** | 0.868 |
| 60-day | 13 | **+2.09%** | 15% | +1.30% | 25% | **+0.53** | 0.811 |

**LQD (investment-grade credit)**

| horizon | n | cond. mean | cond. P[down] | base mean | base P[down] | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 13 | **−0.51%** | 46% | +0.08% | 43% | **−1.65** | 0.029 |
| 20-day | 13 | **+1.00%** | 46% | +0.33% | 39% | **+0.59** | 0.886 |
| 60-day | 13 | **+2.61%** | 23% | +0.99% | 34% | **+1.00** | 0.954 |

Read it carefully. At **5 days** there *is* a faint bearish tilt — every asset's
conditional mean is below its base rate and the *t* is negative (LQD strongest at
**−1.65**, placebo *p* = 0.029) — exactly the "the plumbing is seizing" story. But **none
clears |t| ≥ 2**, and the effect is gone within a month: at **20 and 60 days the sign
flips** — SPY is **+1.95% / +5.21%** (*above* base), credit higher too. The repo spike is
not followed by a sell-off; it is followed by a **relief rally**, because the spike is what
triggers the Fed/ official backstop. The "warning" inverts at horizon.

## The episodes themselves — the punchline is the famous ones

SPY 20-day forward return (1-day lag) after each named episode:

| episode | SPY +20d | episode | SPY +20d |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| year-end-2018 | +7.89% | year-end-2021 | −5.18% |
| quarter-end-2019Q1 | +2.87% | quarter-end-2022Q3 | +5.35% |
| **sept-2019** (THE one) | **−0.44%** | **svb-mar-2023** | **+6.73%** |
| year-end-2019 | −0.97% | quarter-end-2023Q3 | −2.74% |
| **covid-mar-2020** | **+10.52%** | quarter-end-2024Q3 | +2.31% |
| quarter-end-2020Q3 | −2.09% | year-end-2024 | +2.25% |
| quarter-end-2025Q1 | −1.15% | | |

The iconic **September 2019** spike was followed by SPY essentially **flat** (−0.44% over a
month). The one episode everyone "remembers" as a crash — **March 2020** — was the COVID
*bottom*: SPY rose **+10.52%** over the next month, and **SVB 2023** rose **+6.73%**. The
crashes attributed to repo were either coincident with the spike (you couldn't have acted)
or a *buying* opportunity, not a warning to flee.

## "De-risk on the spike" — the rule loses money past a week

| horizon | n trades | gross avoided loss | net @ 5 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 13 | +0.71% | +0.66% |
| 20-day | 13 | **−1.95%** | **−2.00%** |
| 60-day | 13 | **−5.21%** | **−5.26%** |

De-risking SPY on the spike "avoids" a tiny +0.71% over 5 days (inside the noise) and then
**costs you 2–5%** at 20/60 days, because you sold into the rebound. Costs (5 bps) are
irrelevant — the rule is wrong-signed past a week, and at **13 trades in 16.5 years** it
could never be a NAV-scale strategy anyway.

## Robustness — the systemic-only subset makes it *worse*

Dropping the routine quarter/year-end turns and keeping only the three headline *systemic*
crises (Sept 2019, COVID Mar-2020, SVB Mar-2023):

| horizon | n | cond. mean | base mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 3 | −0.46% | +0.29% | −0.45 | 0.247 |
| 20-day | 3 | +5.60% | +1.16% | +1.38 | 0.980 |
| 60-day | 3 | **+12.18%** | +3.41% | **+2.18** | 0.992 |

The "purest" repo crises give the **strongest** result — in the *wrong direction* for a
bearish warning: at 60 days SPY is **+12.18%** after the three systemic spikes (*t* = +2.18
toward *gains*). The only horizon/subset that reaches |t| ≥ 2 says **buy**, not sell.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and small samples are weak

A deterministic risk-asset tape with **13 stress dates** planted by construction and a
controllable forward edge:

| planted 20-day edge | n | cond. 20d mean | base 20d mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 13 | −0.93% | +0.27% | −0.88 | 0.191 |
| **−0.08** (large bearish edge) | 13 | −8.20% | −0.24% | **−6.28** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted edge the test does **not** cross |t| = 2 (a dozen events can't
manufacture significance even when noise tilts the point estimate down). Only a **huge**
planted bearish edge — −8% over a month — drives *t* to −6.3. The control proves two things
at once: the measurement engine is unbiased, **and** ~a dozen events is too few to detect
any edge of plausible magnitude. That is the entire lesson.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The 5-day tilt is real-as-a-whisper and correctly signed (cond < base,
  *t* ≈ −1 to −1.7) but **fails the |t| ≥ 2 bar**, evaporates within a month, and **flips to
  *positive*** at 20/60 days. The signal is a **curated event list**, not a live tape, and on
  the systemic-only subset the only significant result points the *wrong way*. Funding-stress
  proxy + no robust *t* ⇒ **NONE**, not REAL.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** "De-risk on the spike" earns a noise-level +0.66% net at 5 days
  and then **loses 2–5%** at 20/60 days. **13 trades in 16.5 years** (the famous systemic ones:
  ~once every few years) can't be a NAV-scale strategy, and the rule is wrong-signed where it
  would matter. Gone the moment you hold past a week.
- **"Repo spike = flee risk"? — BUSTED.** A handful of named episodes in a market that rises
  most months *will* look ominous around the spike and then rebound — because the spike is the
  thing that summons the backstop. Sept 2019 was flat; March 2020 and SVB were *bottoms*. The
  "watch the repo market" oracle is a **sample-size + confounding mirage** (the systemic crash
  everyone cites, March 2020, is COVID, not repo).
